summary: Tipperary man transported to New South Wales after the 1834 killing of a constable at Ballynonty; John's 4th-great-grand-uncle.
bio: Patrick Heffernan was probably a son of Humphrey Heffernan and Anastasia Ryan. In 1834 he and his brother James were convicted over the killing of Constable Feeney at Ballynonty. Patrick was first sentenced to life, and like his brother was transported to New South Wales. There he married twice and raised eleven children. He died at Orange, New South Wales, on 10 December 1869. He is John's 4th-great-grand-uncle, and should not be confused with the older Patrick Heffernan (1763–1871) in the family.
sources: Michael Dwyer, Heffernans of Slieveardagh (Welsh Hill Press, 2020), Branch 4 (and Branch 3), working from the Killenaule and Gortnahoe Catholic parish registers: https://archive.org/details/heffernans-of-slieveardagh (citing NSW death certificate 5288/1869)
